subject.title: feat(memory-core): skip tool construction for dreaming narrative subagent runs (no-tools mode from #93756 review guidance)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `disableTools` in the Gateway and plugin subagent contracts while reserving successful use to server-created plugin-runtime clients?
rationale: The implementation needs schema visibility to traverse the closed Gateway request object, but the resulting API is intentionally asymmetric: external clients can express it and are rejected, while server-owned plugins can use it.

options.title: Approve the reserved plugin capability
options.body: Accept the guarded `disableTools` field as the shared plugin-to-runner capability because it implements the earlier no-tools guidance without adding user configuration.

options.title: Narrow the transport contract
options.body: Require a different internal plugin dispatch mechanism if maintainers do not want this option represented in the public Gateway protocol model.

recommendation.title: Approve the reserved plugin capability
recommendation.body: Accept the guarded `disableTools` field as the shared plugin-to-runner capability because it implements the earlier no-tools guidance without adding user configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: Their earlier related Dream Diary proposal and its closing review are the supplied provenance for the requested no-tools direction; shared-runtime owners should be included if the contract is accepted.
